samples.summary: The new row-height clamp does not close the paginator hang: `LayoutTable.rowHeights[r]` is also derived from cell content height, and an unvalidated `fontSize`/`padding`/`image.height` CRDT attribute still makes `while (consumed < rowHeight)` non-terminating for every reader
samples.evidence:
The delta's stated threat is "an `Infinity` height never terminates and a `1e9` one builds a million pages" (row-height.ts:20-29), and it clamps only the *user-specified minimum* at table-layout.ts:253 (step 5b raises the row height, never lowers it). The row height the paginator actually consumes is also produced by step 3/4 from cell content: `cellHeight = lines.reduce(...) + padding * 2` (table-layout.ts:196) → `rowHeights[r] = Math.max(rowHeights[r], cell.height)` (table-layout.ts:213). Those inputs are read from CRDT attributes with no bound at all:
  • `style.fontSize = Number(attrs.fontSize)` — packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:72 and the frontend twin packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:192
  • `style.padding = Number(attrs.padding)` — crdt-tree.ts:131 / yorkie-doc-store.ts:311
  • `image.height` is checked finite but unbounded — crdt-tree.ts:80-86 (1e9 is accepted)
  • block `lineHeight` is checked finite but unbounded — crdt-attrs.ts:137-138, used as `Math.max(1, resolved.lineHeight) * maxFontSize` at layout.ts:874-878.
Attack: a collaborator (or any client that can PUT doc content) writes `fontSize="Infinity"` on an inline node inside a table cell, or `padding="Infinity"` on the cell node. Reader path: treeNodeToBlock → parseInlineStyle/parseCellStyle → Infinity → `ptToPx(Infinity)` = Infinity → line.height = Infinity → cell.height = Infinity → `rowHeights[r] = Infinity` (untouched by step 5b) → pagination.ts:99 `currentY + rowHeight <= contentHeight` is false → pagination.ts:124 `while (consumed < Infinity)`: each iteration `fragHeight = Math.min(remaining, pageAvail)` = one content height, so `consumed` grows by ~864 forever while a `startNewPage()`/`PageLine` is pushed per iteration → hang and unbounded memory growth in every reader's tab (and in any Node-side paginating export). A finite `fontSize="1e9"` or `image.height=1e9` gives the ~1.1M-page OOM variant. The poisoned attribute persists in the CRDT, so every reload re-hangs. The new test (test/model/row-height.test.ts:88-110) only exercises `tableData.rowHeights`, so it reads as covering the loop while the loop stays reachable. The loop itself has no defensive bound (`if (!Number.isFinite(rowHeight))` / a page-count cap), which is where this class would actually be closed.

The neighbouring numeric attributes read in the same functions have no equivalent: crdt-tree.ts:72 (`fontSize = Number(...)`, so `NaN`/`Infinity`/1e9 all reach layout), crdt-tree.ts:131 (`padding = Number(...)`), crdt-tree.ts:80-86 (`image.width/height` finite-checked but unbounded), crdt-attrs.ts:135-139 (`lineHeight`/`marginTop`/`marginLeft` finite-checked but unbounded). samples.summary: The v1 docs content ingest validates `tableData.columnWidths`/`rows` but not `tableData.rowHeights`, so a non-array value reaches `.map()` in the tree writer and throws an unhandled TypeError (500)
samples.evidence: `assertValidBlock` checks `Array.isArray(td.columnWidths)` and `Array.isArray(td.rows)` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:449-454) but never inspects `td.rowHeights`. The writer then does `if (block.tableData.rowHeights && block.tableData.rowHeights.length > 0) { ...rowHeights.map((h) => h ?? '').join(',') }` (docs-tree.ts:158-161). A body with `"rowHeights": "abc"` (or `{"length":2}`) passes validation, has a truthy `.length > 0`, and has no `.map` → TypeError escapes the controller as a 500 instead of a 400. String entries containing commas also inject extra positions into the comma-joined attribute. The delta's own docstring notes the backend "serializes whatever it is handed" (row-height.ts:16-17) but adds no ingest-side check, so this stays a request-scoped crash / delimiter-shift for any client with doc write access.

samples.summary: MAX_ROW_HEIGHT = 10000 still permits ~12 pages per table row, and nothing caps total page count, so the amplification is reduced rather than removed
samples.evidence: With `MAX_ROW_HEIGHT = 10000` against a letter content height of ~864 px, one poisoned row yields ~12 pages from the pagination.ts:124 split loop, and nested tables sum clamped child rows into an outer row height far above the band (table-layout.ts:196/213 via layoutCellBlocks' nested `totalHeight`). A table of a few thousand cheap row nodes therefore still produces tens of thousands of `LayoutPage`s. A cap on total pages (or on `LayoutTable.totalHeight`) alongside the per-row band would bound the reader-side cost independently of how the height was derived.

verdict.reason: The described code is present as claimed and unguarded. `pagination.ts:124` iterates `while (consumed < rowHeight)` with no finiteness check or page cap, advancing `consumed` by at most one content height per iteration (`:127-134`) while pushing a page each time (`:125,137-146`). The `rowHeight` it consumes is `LayoutTable.rowHeights[ri]` (`:95`), which is produced from cell content at `table-layout.ts:196` (`cellHeight = lines.reduce(...) + padding * 2`) and `:213` (`Math.max(rowHeights[r], cell.height)`). The new clamp at `table-layout.ts:251-258` calls `normalizeRowHeight` only on the *user-specified* `tableData.rowHeights[r]` and only raises the height (`userHeight > rowHeights[r]`), so a content-derived `Infinity`/`1e9` is untouched; steps 5c/6 (`:293-295`, `:300-306`) likewise only grow it, and no clamp exists before the return at `:324-333`. The feeding attributes are parsed without bound: `crdt-tree.ts:72` (`fontSize = Number(attrs.fontSize)`), `crdt-tree.ts:131` (`padding = Number(attrs.padding)`), mirrored in the live reader at `yorkie-doc-store.ts:192,311`; `crdt-tree.ts:80-86` accepts any finite `image.height`. The height math is unclamped end-to-end: `layout.ts:124-135` (`ptToPx(fontSize)`) and `layout.ts:874-887` (`line.height = lineHeightMultiplier * maxFontSize`, no ceiling). So a collaborator (or any client able to write doc content) can persist `fontSize="Infinity"` on an inline inside a table cell and hang/OOM every reader's paginate pass on each load — a persistent cross-user denial of service from unvalidated untrusted input, which the delta's own comment (`row-height.ts:20-29`) identifies as the threat it meant to close. I found no guard rendering it unreachable.

verdict.reason: The absence is real and I found no counterexample anywhere. crdt-tree.ts:72 reads `fontSize` with a bare `Number()` (not even a finite check) and :131 does the same for cell `padding`; crdt-attrs.ts:135-139 finite-checks `lineHeight`/`marginTop`/`marginLeft` but applies no ceiling; the mirrored live reader repeats all three (yorkie-doc-store.ts:192, :203, :311). No band for any of them exists on any read path: repo-wide there is no MAX_FONT_SIZE/MAX_PADDING analogue, the only font-size clamp is the UI widget in font-catalog.ts:73-83 (reached via editor.ts:1282's caller-supplied clamp, not the CRDT boundary), the paste sanitizer clipboard.ts:69-70/130-143/234 is finite-only with no ceiling, the backend serializer docs-tree.ts:85 does not validate, and pagination.ts has no page-count cap. The vector is the same one normalizeRowHeight documents: an attacker with collaborator write access sets cell `padding` (or `fontSize`) to 1e9, table-layout.ts:196 computes cellHeight = sum(line.height) + padding*2, :213 promotes it into rowHeights, and pagination.ts:124's `while (consumed < rowHeight)` advances at most contentHeight (~900px) per iteration, building ~2M pages and LayoutLines — a hang/OOM for every other reader, including the read-only revision-preview path. That entry bypasses the new guard entirely, so the invariant asserted in the comment at table-layout.ts:246-250 ("bounding it here bounds all of them") is false. Untrusted collaborator input reaching geometry unvalidated is in the security lane (unsafe input handling / resource exhaustion), and the impact is cross-user denial of service, so major is the right severity.

finding.summary: The read boundary this change hardens for `listLevel` still passes `tableData.rowHeights` through a bare `Number(...)`, and an attacker-chosen row height makes the paginator's row-split loop iterate essentially without bound — a persistent hang/OOM for every reader of the document.
finding.evidence: This diff adds `normalizeListLevel` at `treeNodeToBlock` (crdt-tree.ts:249-250) precisely because "a peer's Tree attribute is read straight through `Number(...)`" and every downstream reader multiplies it into geometry. Forty lines above the new clamp, the same function reads row heights with no validation: `attrs.rowHeights.split(',').map(v => (v === '' ? undefined : Number(v)))` (crdt-tree.ts:195-199); the frontend twin does the same at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:453-455. That value is then adopted verbatim as a row minimum — `if (userHeight !== undefined && userHeight > rowHeights[r]) rowHeights[r] = userHeight;` (packages/docs/src/view/table-layout.ts:245-251), with no ceiling — and reaches the paginator's split loop `while (consumed < rowHeight) { ... consumed += fragHeight; }` (packages/docs/src/view/pagination.ts:124-146), where `fragHeight` is capped at one page's `contentHeight` (~900px) and each iteration pushes a `PageLine` and starts a new page. Attack: any principal with write access to the doc — a collaborator on the shared Yorkie tree, or an API key with write scope via `PUT /api/v1/.../content` whose docs validator checks only `Array.isArray(tableData.rows/columnWidths)` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:449-454) — stores `tableData.rowHeights: [1e12]` on one table block. `writeDocsRoot`/`buildBlockNode` serializes it verbatim (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:158-162), so it persists; every other client's `paginate()` then loops ~1e9 times allocating pages until the tab dies, and the same code path is used by the PDF export/CLI. Same threat model the diff's own comments invoke ("one hostile collaborator could blank the rendered document ... for every other reader"), reached through the attribute next door instead of `listLevel`. I traced the chain in source but did not execute it, hence medium confidence.

verdict.reason: The finding claims rowHeights passes through a bare `Number(...)` at three read boundaries with "no ceiling", enabling an unbounded paginator loop. All three cited locations actually call `normalizeRowHeight`: crdt-tree.ts:203 (`normalizeRowHeight(Number(v))`), yorkie-doc-store.ts:460 (same, imported at :51), and table-layout.ts:253 (`const userHeight = normalizeRowHeight(tableData.rowHeights[r])`) — the exact opposite of the quoted evidence. normalizeRowHeight (row-height.ts:35-39) returns undefined for non-finite or <=0 values and clamps via `Math.min(MAX_ROW_HEIGHT, raw)` with MAX_ROW_HEIGHT=10000 (row-height.ts:8). The attacker payload 1e12 therefore becomes 10000, and pagination.ts:124-146's `while (consumed < rowHeight)` loop terminates in ~11 iterations against a ~900px contentHeight rather than ~1e9. The LayoutTable.rowHeights array pagination consumes is produced only by computeTableLayout (table-layout.ts:204, clamped at :253), so a hostile value persisted by the backend ingest is still neutralized on every read before reaching the split loop. The code is not as described.
